<!-- pr-reviewer: c0fbedc9a71053538d7a88f6e512b4577fb5a75d -->
**Verdict: the PR's own change is clean, but it cannot merge yet.** It is the top of the stack #1137 -> #1219 -> #1301 and can only merge after #1137 and #1219 (retarget to `main` first, per the stacking law). It also conflicts with current `main` today, and #1219's head has moved since this branch took it.

## What looks good
- Reviewed #1301's own delta against #1219's `0d3a6a21` (15 files, +413/-11). The R-plane check is additive: `ThreadParams::validate` still runs every earlier law (finite, top/link-plane, per-hole), and the new `r_z` block sits before the per-hole loop without touching it. `None` keeps the #894 ride, so no existing golden moved (golden_cl 32/32).
- Fails closed: R below any feature's top, R above the link plane, and a non-finite R are refused by name in the kernel (`thread_mill.rs`, `validate`) and never clamped. `HolePlan` uses `r_z.max(top).max(run_out)`, so the rapid is never lower than the old ride.
- The door (`thread_r_plane::door`) also refuses a NaN R plane, and runs after the tool/feature laws so their wording is unchanged. The stock law (`thread_r_plane::judge`) runs before the #992/#985 way-in laws, which stay in place.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside tests in the new code; provenance lines present; files stay under 400 lines (`thread_mill.rs` 334, `thread_op.rs` 333).
- `r_z: None` added to `thread_boss_tests.rs`, `hole_wall_flats.rs`, `golden_cl.rs`, `thread_pass_tests.rs`: pure struct-field fill, behaviour-neutral (those suites pass unchanged).
- No `Cargo`, `build.rs`, `.github`, scripts or process files in the delta, so it was built.

## Local results (PR head; a merge with `main` was not possible, see Conflict)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-motion --lib thread` | 15 passed |
| `camcraft-app --lib thread` | 20 passed |
| app `thread_entry` 8, `thread_boss` 12, `thread_mill` 8, `thread_mill_rim` 11, `thread_passes` 4, `hole_wall_flats` 5 | all pass |
| app `golden_cl` 32, `solid_law_goldens` 7, `mcp -- thread` 3 | all pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

**Mutation checks** (each change reverted afterwards):
- Killed: kernel R-below-top refusal, R-above-link refusal, finiteness check, `rapid_z` honouring R, `kernel_params` passing `r_z`, the `judge` call in `generate.rs`, the `judge` comparison, the `judge` disc radius, the door's second call site, the door comparison.
- Survived (non-blocking, see notes): the door call on the "pitch not stated yet" early-return path in `thread_op.rs`; the `judge` filter that skips non-dive rapids.

## Conflict
`git merge upstream/main` conflicts in `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` (`startPreamble`: this chain's `spinRev ? "M4" : "M3"` against main's `spindleOn = true` from #1372). That hunk is not in #1301's own delta; it comes from the chain below. `mergeable` reads `CONFLICTING` (read twice), so the `conflicts` label is accurate. Whoever re-merges `main` should keep both: `block(["S" + ni(sRpm), spinRev ? "M4" : "M3"]); spindleOn = true;`. This is a post-script safety-adjacent hunk, so please check it rather than take it blindly.

Also note: this branch carries #1137 at `4f15b9b3` and #1219 at `0d3a6a21`. #1137 is now `875ea081` and #1219 is `3af7914b` (under rework), so a delta re-check of #1301 is needed once the parents settle.

## Requested before merge
1. Land #1137 and #1219 first, then retarget this PR to `main`, merge `main`, and resolve `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` as above.
2. Re-merge the moved parent heads and re-run the thread suites.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)
- The new golden `thread_mill_raised_r_plane.cl` is justified (R 2 mm over the tops; first golden to pin a raised plane) and is compared byte for byte in `golden_cl`. It is not judged by `solid_law_goldens`: that file's `thread_verdicts` covers only the two M8 multi-form goldens, as for the other thread goldens. The raised-R program is instead generated, verified clean and posted through the gate by `thread_entry::the_operations_r_plane_is_where_the_rapid_stops_and_the_feed_starts`, which fails when `r_z` is dropped. The PR text's wording on this is fine; just don't expect a `solid_law_goldens` entry.
- Gap: add a one-line test that `door` refuses a low fixed R plane while the pitch is still unstated (the early-return branch in `thread_op.rs` is unpinned). The generator would still refuse later, so this is cosmetic.
- Behaviour change worth a release-note line: with the default R (Top of Model), existing thread ops on a hole or boss whose mouth stands above the model top are now refused at create/edit/generate (the two MCP fixtures had to move for this). It fails closed and names the fix, which is the intended design.
- The `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #1212`, decision record and `r_z` fixture changes all look right.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
